name: Merriepetals
body:
The merriepetals are a species of brilliantly emotional plant creatures. Theories speculate that they were created by the fey, or were created to control fey, or were created by the gods as guardians of natural beauty. Whichever theory is correct, the original plan for these beautiful creatures has gone fantastically awry.

Physical Description: Merriepetals are delicate floral beings, possessing only the barest implications of humanoid form in their shape. In their movement, though, they are deeply human, walking and gesturing like particularly emphatic ballet dancers. Because of these gesticulations, Merriepetals are quite easy to read despite their lack of true faces. Merriepetals resemble colorful halfling-sized flowers, with petite stems for legs and petals or leaves for torso and arms. The main bloom always comprises the head, though the type of flower varies from thistles to roses to morning glories. Merriepetals are always surrounded by a cloying smell that is difficult to place. They weigh 15-25 pounds.

Society: Many merriepetals remain in the meadows and prairies of their birthplace, partaking in endless dances and revelries. Others venture out into civilization, for merriepetals love to learn more about humanoids. Still other merriepetals join darker circles and drag humanoids and fey into their revels, willingly or no. Their spores make these abductions disturbingly easy to accomplish.

Relations: Merriepetals are fascinated by the lives of the “beasts,” as they call all non-plant species. Although reproduction is a very dispassionate and passive process for the flower beings, romance is not, and romantic relationships between the lively merriepetals and humanoids are almost as common as those that stay entirely confined to the species. They deal most often with elves and gnomes as fellow nature-lovers, and tend to form especially close bonds with the latter—gnomes sometimes live among merriepetals, and vice versa. Dwarves generally regard merriepetals as troublemakers. Half-elves and half-orcs who deal with merriepetals often develop followings, for the creatures are enamored with the “romantic flair” of someone torn between two worlds. Halflings and humans, on the other hand, are the most common targets of the less kindly merriepetals abductions, and so tend to be superstitiously uninformed about merriepetals’ true nature.

Alignment and Religion: Merriepetals are melodramatic and expressive by nature, but have few moral tendencies one way or the other. They tend strongly towards chaotic alignments. They worship deities of beauty and love, but evil merriepetals embrace decidedly darker aspects. They bear a strange cultural mistrust for deities of lust, who are oft-cast in their songs as selfish tricksters and mischief-makers.

Adventurers: Merriepetals love grand journeys, particularly the kinds that allow them to meet many different people. As such, they are unlikely to delve dungeons alone, but are drawn to matters of intrigue and mystery like moths to candlelight.

Core Traits (13 RP)
Ability Score Modifiers: Merriepetals are graceful and possessed of truly magnetic personalities, but they are frail and have very little self-control. They gain +2 Dexterity, +2 Charisma, –2 Constitution, and –4 Wisdom. –2 RP
Type: Merriepetals are Plant creatures. They need not sleep, but can gain the benefits of rest as normal. They gain all normal plant immunities, except that they are not immune to poison or polymorph effects, and they are treated as humanoids for the purposes of being targeted by mind-affecting effects. 7 RP
Size: Merriepetals are Small creatures and gain a +1 size bonus to their AC, a +1 size bonus on attack rolls, a –1 penalty on their combat maneuver checks and to Combat Maneuver Defense, and a +4 size bonus on Stealth checks.
Speed: Merriepetals have a base speed of 20 feet.
Languages: Merriepetals begin play speaking Common and Sylvan. Merriepetals with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following: Elven, Gnome, Halfling, Orc, and Treant.
Other Traits
Performer: Merriepetals gain a +1 racial bonus on Perform (dance) and another Perform skill of their choice, and these are always class skills. 2 RP
Hallucinogenic Spores (Ex) For 10 minutes each day, a merriepetal can release spores that contain powerful narcotic chemicals. This duration does not need to be consecutive, but it must be spent in 1 minute increments. The merriepetal can suppress or activate this aura as a move action. The spores are far too small to see with the naked eye. While the spores are active, creatures within 5 feet of the merriepetal take 1 Wisdom damage at the start of their turn unless they succeed at a Will save (DC 10 + 1/2 HD + Charisma modifier). A merriepetal is immune to its own spores. Due to the subtlety of the toxins, the target must make their save by 5 or more to notice any adverse effects. If this Wisdom damage would equal or exceed the creature’s Wisdom score, it takes no further damage from this ability for 24 hours and is instead affected by charm monster until at least 2 points of this Wisdom damage are healed. This is a mind-affecting poison effect. 6 RP
Treespeech: Merriepetals have the ability to converse with plants as if subject to a continual speak with plants spell. 2 RP
Frost Vulnerability: Merriepetals take a –2 penalty on Fortitude saves to avoid nonlethal damage from cold environments. They have vulnerability to cold. –2 RP
Alternate Racial Traits

The following racial traits may be selected instead of existing merriepetal traits.

Dried Herbs: Not all merriepetals resemble fresh blossoms. Some merriepetals are quite crackly and dry. These merriepetals gain vulnerability to fire and take a –2 penalty on Fortitude saves to avoid nonlethal damage from hot environments. This replaces frost vulnerability.
Poison Mixer: Some merriepetals generate their hallucinogens in a stronger nectar form, rather than as spores. Three times per day as a swift action, the merriepetal can create a poison that can be applied to a weapon or fed to a helpless or willing (or unknowing) target. The poison loses its potency after 10 minutes. Merriepetals with this trait do not gain the hallucinogenic spores trait.
Merriepetal Nectar: Imbibed or weapon—ingested or injury; save Fort DC 10 + 1/2 the merriepetal’s Hit Dice + its Charisma modifier; frequency 1/round for 6 rounds; effect 1d3 Wisdom damage; cure 2 saves; special If this Wisdom damage would equal or exceed the target’s Wisdom score, it is instead charmed, see hallucinogenic spores
Thorny Dancer: Some thistle and rose merriepetals have particularly long and sharp thorns, and tend to be confronted with a difficulty in getting close to others as a result. Any creature striking a thorny merriepetal with a melee weapon, an unarmed strike, or a natural weapon takes 1d3 points of piercing damage. Creatures using reach weapons are not damaged. Creatures that successfully grapple a merriepetal take 1d6 points of piercing damage. In addition, the merriepetal’s natural attacks and unarmed strikes deal an additional 1d3 points of piercing damage. This replaces hallucinogenic spores.
Wandering Exile: Some merriepetals tire of their constant revels, and instead travel, learning about the outside world. These merriepetals gain a +1 racial bonus to Knowledge (geography) and one other Knowledge skill of their choice, and these are always class skills for the merriepetal. This trait replaces performer.
